A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ERMAR research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated content. V2's appendix ends at A.4; v3 extends through A.8.

before.justification: V2 reports original ERMAR perplexity, in-context learning accuracy, memory and latency measurements, and ablation results in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds experiments on retrieval size, pruning strategies, and embedding dimensionality.

M1.justification: The core architecture, relevance scoring, RSAR retrieval rule, objective, and memory-update equations are retained. V3 expands the workflow explanation and documents a 10/80/10 pruning heuristic, but does not establish that this replaces an earlier implemented procedure. The conflicting hidden-dimension report is assessed under experimental settings and documentation.

E1.justification: Training remains on SlimPajama; evaluation retains WikiText-103, PG-19, Proof-Pile, SST-2, MR, Subj, SST-5, and MPQA. The new sensitivity experiments vary configurations within existing task coverage. The customer-support example already appears in v2 and remains illustrative.

E2.justification: The comparator membership in the main language-modeling and ICL comparisons is unchanged. Appendix A.7 adds Uniform, Recency-only, Frequency-only, and alternative hybrid pruning ratios as evaluated comparators to the proposed 10-80-10 strategy in Tables 13–14.

E3.justification: Appendices A.6–A.8 introduce controlled sweeps of Top-K values 1–32, eleven pruning strategies, and embedding dimensions 512/1024/2048, with specified context lengths and demonstration configurations. Existing benchmark splits, metrics, and appendix training settings remain stable. Section 3.1.2 nevertheless changes the reported hidden dimension from 3200 to 100, without explaining whether the actual configuration changed.

E4.justification: V3 substantially expands sensitivity analysis: A.6 tests retrieval breadth against efficiency and perplexity; A.7 tests pruning criteria and ratios; A.8 tests embedding dimensionality against ICL accuracy. Existing embedder and reranking ablations and the fine-grained context analysis are retained. A.5 only visualizes the existing Table 9 results.

E5.justification: Both versions report latency standard deviations in Table 5. New Tables 10 and 14 continue this reporting practice without adding disclosed run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Additional uncertainty-bearing result rows do not establish a changed statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces ERMAR's WikiText-103 perplexities at 1K/2K/4K/16K from 7.92/7.41/7.34/7.08 to 8.42/7.61/7.62/7.80 without explaining the revision. Tables 10–15 add efficiency and accuracy findings from the new sensitivity experiments. Tables 2–9 retain their numerical results. The PG-19 4K-to-16K degradation statement is corrected from 3.2% to 0.31%.

T1.justification: The original mathematical formulation is retained, reordered, and more extensively numbered. Added symbol explanations and the standard attention-weighted value expression clarify the existing mechanism; they introduce no substantive new theory, assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central contributions. The conclusion adds quantified headline claims, including a 3.2% perplexity reduction, 6.1%/7.1% ICL improvements, and up to 30% lower reserved memory, giving computational efficiency greater prominence. These claims are not all clearly reconciled with the tables.

C2.justification: V3 newly interprets 16K underperformance as a reranking-overhead and training-boundary tradeoff. Its appendix argues that retrieval breadth and pruning ratios chiefly affect efficiency, recommends K=4–8 and context-dependent pruning, and attributes benefits of 512-dimensional embeddings to reduced noise and redundancy. These substantially extend practical and mechanistic interpretation; the formal limitations remain essentially unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 adds concrete pruning criteria, PCA reduction and dimensional-padding details, a promised code-release location, and the compute-cluster name. Most appendix implementation settings are retained. However, it reverses the explicit hidden-size correction and removes experiment-specific GPU descriptions from Table 1 and the memory/latency discussion, reducing some documentation precision.

R1.justification: The cited-work membership and substantive positioning relative to MemLong, retrieval-augmented models, and learning-to-rank methods remain unchanged. Section 2.1 is shortened without materially changing that positioning.

P1.justification: V3 extensively rewrites the method walkthrough, results discussion, and conclusion. It merges architecture and configuration subsections, reorganizes efficiency and ablation discussions under Section 3.2, expands explanatory prose, and repairs appendix references. Author information changes and acknowledgments are added.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are revised with expanded captions; Figures 3 and 5 newly visualize retained Tables 4 and 9. The original fine-grained plot remains unchanged as Figure 4. Six appendix tables are added, and Tables 7–8 become compact single-column displays. Figure 3's caption reverses the color assignments shown in its legend.

improvement.justification: V3 improves explanation and adds useful sensitivity studies, but also introduces material reporting problems. It reverses v2's hidden-size correction, leaves revised Table 1 values unexplained, and introduces conflicting latency units in Tables 10 and 14. Its new claim of uniformly superior WikiText-103 performance contradicts Phi3's lower perplexities in Table 1. These reliability problems complicate the value of the added analysis, preventing a confident net quality judgment.
